sanskrit: eko 'pasṛtya cedibhyaḥ pāṇḍavān yaḥ samāśritaḥ dhṛṣṭaketuṃ tam āyāntaṃ droṇāt kaḥ samavārayat
english: Who held off from Droṇa that Dhṛṣṭaketu as he came on—he who, alone, broke away from the Cedis and gave his allegiance to the Pāṇḍavas?

sanskrit: yo 'vadhīt ketumāñ śūro rājaputraṃ sudarśanam aparāntagiridvāre kas taṃ droṇād avārayat
english: That brave Ketumat who slew the prince Sudarśana at the gateway of the western mountains—who kept him back from Droṇa?

sanskrit: strīpūrvo yo naravyāghro yaḥ sa veda guṇāguṇān śikhaṇḍinaṃ yājñasenim amlānamanasaṃ yudhi
english: That tiger among men, once a woman, who knows men's merits and faults—Śikhaṇḍin, son of Yajñasena, unflinching in heart upon the field—

sanskrit: devavratasya samare hetuṃ mṛtyor mahātmanaḥ droṇāyābhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ ke vīrāḥ paryavārayan
english: the appointed cause of the death in battle of high-souled Devavrata—as he advanced straight upon Droṇa, what heroes hemmed him in?

sanskrit: yasminn abhyadhikā vīre guṇāḥ sarve dhanaṃjayāt yasminn astrāṇi satyaṃ ca brahmacaryaṃ ca nityadā
english: That hero in whom all virtues surpass even those of Dhanaṃjaya, in whom dwell forever the celestial weapons, truth, and continence—

sanskrit: vāsudevasamaṃ vīrye dhanaṃjayasamaṃ bale tejasādityasadṛśaṃ bṛhaspatisamaṃ matau
english: the equal of Vāsudeva in valor, the equal of Dhanaṃjaya in strength, like the sun in splendor, like Bṛhaspati in wisdom—

sanskrit: abhimanyuṃ mahātmānaṃ vyāttānanam ivāntakam droṇāyābhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ ke vīrāḥ paryavārayan
english: the high-souled Abhimanyu, like the Ender with gaping jaws—as he advanced straight upon Droṇa, what heroes hemmed him in?

sanskrit: taruṇas tv aruṇaprakhyaḥ saubhadraḥ paravīrahā yadābhyādravata droṇaṃ tadāsīd vo manaḥ katham
english: When the youthful son of Subhadrā, glowing like the dawn, slayer of enemy heroes, charged upon Droṇa—how then stood your hearts?

sanskrit: draupadeyā naravyāghrāḥ samudram iva sindhavaḥ yad droṇam ādravan saṃkhye ke vīrās tān avārayan
english: When the sons of Draupadī, those tigers among men, rushed upon Droṇa in battle like rivers upon the sea, what heroes turned them back?

sanskrit: ye te dvādaśa varṣāṇi krīḍām utsṛjya bālakāḥ astrārtham avasan bhīṣme bibhrato vratam uttamam
english: Those boys who for twelve years forsook all play and, keeping the highest vow, dwelt with Bhīṣma for the sake of mastering arms—

sanskrit: kṣatraṃjayaḥ kṣatradevaḥ kṣatradharmā ca māninaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnātmajā vīrāḥ ke tān droṇād avārayan
english: Kṣatraṃjaya, Kṣatradeva, and proud Kṣatradharman, heroic sons of Dhṛṣṭadyumna—who kept them back from Droṇa?

sanskrit: śatād viśiṣṭaṃ yaṃ yuddhe samapaśyanta vṛṣṇayaḥ cekitānaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ kas taṃ droṇād avārayat
english: That mighty archer Cekitāna, whom the Vṛṣṇis reckoned in battle worth more than a hundred men—who kept him back from Droṇa?

sanskrit: vārdhakṣemiḥ kaliṅgānāṃ yaḥ kanyām āharad yudhi anādhṛṣṭir adīnātmā kas taṃ droṇād avārayat
english: Anādhṛṣṭi, son of Vṛddhakṣema, undaunted in soul, who carried off the maiden of the Kaliṅgas by force of arms—who kept him back from Droṇa?

sanskrit: bhrātaraḥ pañca kaikeyā dhārmikāḥ satyavikramāḥ indragopakavarṇāś ca raktavarmāyudhadhvajāḥ
english: The five Kaikeya brothers, righteous men of truthful valor, of the hue of the cochineal insect, with crimson armor, weapons, and banners—

sanskrit: mātṛṣvasuḥ sutā vīrāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ jayārthinaḥ tān droṇaṃ hantum āyātān ke vīrāḥ paryavārayan
english: those heroes, sons of their mother's sister, who sought victory for the Pāṇḍavas—as they came on to slay Droṇa, what heroes hemmed them in?

sanskrit: yaṃ yodhayanto rājāno nājayan vāraṇāvate ṣaṇ māsān abhisaṃrabdhā jighāṃsanto yudhāṃ patim
english: That lord of warriors whom the kings, battling against him at Vāraṇāvata in fury for six months, bent on his death, could not conquer—

sanskrit: dhanuṣmatāṃ varaṃ śūraṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ mahābalam droṇāt kas taṃ naravyāghraṃ yuyutsuṃ pratyavārayat
english: that tiger among men, foremost of bowmen, brave, true to his word, of mighty strength—who held back the eager Yuyutsu from Droṇa?

sanskrit: yaḥ putraṃ kāśirājasya vārāṇasyāṃ mahāratham samare strīṣu gṛdhyantaṃ bhallenāpaharad rathāt
english: He who in battle at Vārāṇasī struck down with a broad-headed shaft from his chariot the great chariot-warrior, the son of the king of Kāśi, as he lusted after the women—

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ pārthānāṃ mantradhāriṇam yuktaṃ duryodhanānarthe sṛṣṭaṃ droṇavadhāya ca
english: that mighty archer Dhṛṣṭadyumna, keeper of the counsels of the Pārthas, bound to Duryodhana's ruin and born for the slaying of Droṇa—

sanskrit: nirdahantaṃ raṇe yodhān dārayantaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ droṇāyābhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ ke vīrāḥ paryavārayan
english: as he burned the warriors in battle and tore them apart on every side, advancing straight upon Droṇa, what heroes hemmed him in?

sanskrit: utsaṅga iva saṃvṛddhaṃ drupadasyāstravittamam śaikhaṇḍinaṃ kṣatradevaṃ ke taṃ droṇād avārayan
english: Kṣatradeva, son of Śikhaṇḍin, most skilled in arms, reared as it were in Drupada's lap—who kept him back from Droṇa?

sanskrit: ya imāṃ pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ carmavat samaveṣṭayat mahatā rathavaṃśena mukhyārighno mahārathaḥ
english: That great chariot-warrior, slayer of the foremost foes, who with his vast line of chariots wrapped this whole earth as in a hide—

sanskrit: daśāśvamedhān ājahre svannapānāptadakṣiṇān nirargalān sarvamedhān putravat pālayan prajāḥ
english: who performed ten horse-sacrifices with abundant food and drink and ample gifts, unhindered and complete, while guarding his people like his own sons—

sanskrit: pibantyo dakṣiṇāṃ yasya gaṅgāsrotaḥ samāpiban tāvatīr gā dadau vīra uśīnarasuto 'dhvare
english: at whose sacrifice the cattle drinking down their fee drank the whole stream of the Gaṅgā—so many cows did that hero, the son of Uśīnara, bestow—

sanskrit: na pūrve nāpare cakrur idaṃ ke cana mānavāḥ iti saṃcukruśur devāḥ kṛte karmaṇi duṣkare
english: "No men of old, nor any to come, have wrought this deed"—so cried the gods aloud when that hard task was done.

sanskrit: paśyāmas triṣu lokeṣu na taṃ saṃsthāsnucāriṣu jātaṃ vāpi janiṣyaṃ vā dvitīyaṃ vāpi saṃprati
english: "Among the still and the moving in the three worlds we see no second to him—neither born before, nor to be born, nor living now."

sanskrit: anyam auśīnarāc chaibyād dhuro voḍhāram ity uta gatiṃ yasya na yāsyanti mānuṣā lokavāsinaḥ
english: "None other than Śaibya, son of Uśīnara, can bear such a yoke"—whose course the men who dwell in the world shall never attain.

sanskrit: tasya naptāram āyāntaṃ śaibyaṃ kaḥ samavārayat droṇāyābhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ vyāttānanam ivāntakam
english: His grandson Śaibya, as he came on—who held him back, advancing straight upon Droṇa like the Ender with gaping jaws?

sanskrit: virāṭasya rathānīkaṃ matsyasyāmitraghātinaḥ prepsantaṃ samare droṇaṃ ke vīrāḥ paryavārayan
english: As the chariot-host of Virāṭa, the Matsya king and slayer of foes, sought to reach Droṇa in battle, what heroes hemmed them in?

sanskrit: sadyo vṛkodarāj jāto mahābalaparākramaḥ māyāvī rākṣaso ghoro yasmān mama mahad bhayam
english: That dread rākṣasa, a master of illusion, of mighty strength and prowess, born in a single day of Vṛkodara, from whom comes my great fear—

sanskrit: pārthānāṃ jayakāmaṃ taṃ putrāṇāṃ mama kaṇṭakam ghaṭotkacaṃ mahābāhuṃ kas taṃ droṇād avārayat
english: the mighty-armed Ghaṭotkaca, longing for the victory of the Pārthas, a thorn in the side of my sons—who kept him back from Droṇa?

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo yeṣām arthāya saṃjaya tyaktāraḥ saṃyuge prāṇān kiṃ teṣām ajitaṃ yudhi
english: These and many others, Saṃjaya, who in their cause would lay down their lives in battle—what could remain unconquered for such men in war?

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ ca puruṣavyāghraḥ śārṅgadhanvā vyapāśrayaḥ hitārthī cāpi pārthānāṃ kathaṃ teṣāṃ parājayaḥ
english: And those whose refuge is that tiger among men, the bearer of the Śārṅga bow, who seeks the good of the Pārthas—how can there be defeat for them?

sanskrit: lokānāṃ gurur atyantaṃ lokanāthaḥ sanātanaḥ nārāyaṇo raṇe nātho divyo divyātmavān prabhuḥ
english: He is the supreme teacher of the worlds, the eternal lord of the worlds, Nārāyaṇa, the protector in battle, divine, of divine essence, the Lord—

sanskrit: yasya divyāni karmāṇi pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ tāny ahaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi bhaktyā sthairyārtham ātmanaḥ
english: whose divine deeds the wise recount; these I shall proclaim with devotion, for the steadying of my own soul.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca śṛṇu divyāni karmāṇi vāsudevasya saṃjaya kṛtavān yāni govindo yathā nānyaḥ pumān kva cit
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Hear the divine deeds of Vāsudeva, Saṃjaya—deeds that Govinda performed as no other man anywhere ever has.

sanskrit: saṃvardhatā gopakule bālenaiva mahātmanā vikhyāpitaṃ balaṃ bāhvos triṣu lokeṣu saṃjaya
english: While yet a child growing up in the herdsmen's clan, the high-souled one made the might of his arms renowned throughout the three worlds, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: uccaiḥśravas tulyabalaṃ vāyuvegasamaṃ jave jaghāna hayarājaṃ yo yamunāvanavāsinam
english: He slew the king of horses that dwelt in the forest by the Yamunā, a steed equal in strength to Uccaiḥśravas and matching the wind in swiftness.

sanskrit: dānavaṃ ghorakarmāṇaṃ gavāṃ mṛtyum ivotthitam vṛṣarūpadharaṃ bālye bhujābhyāṃ nijaghāna ha
english: In his boyhood, with his bare arms, he slew that dānava of dreadful deeds, who had taken the form of a bull and risen up like death itself against the cattle.

sanskrit: pralambaṃ narakaṃ jambhaṃ pīṭhaṃ cāpi mahāsuram muruṃ cācalasaṃkāśam avadhīt puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ
english: The lotus-eyed one slew Pralamba, Naraka, Jambha, the great asura Pīṭha, and Muru, who was like a mountain.

sanskrit: tathā kaṃso mahātejā jarāsaṃdhena pālitaḥ vikrameṇaiva kṛṣṇena sagaṇaḥ śātito raṇe
english: So too Kaṃsa of great splendor, protected by Jarāsaṃdha, was struck down in battle by Kṛṣṇa's prowess alone, together with his followers.

sanskrit: sunāmā nāma vikrāntaḥ samagrākṣauhiṇīpatiḥ bhojarājasya madhyastho bhrātā kaṃsasya vīryavān
english: The valiant Sunāman, lord of a full akṣauhiṇī, a leader among the Bhojas and the mighty brother of Kaṃsa—

sanskrit: baladevadvitīyena kṛṣṇenāmitraghātinā tarasvī samare dagdhaḥ sasainyaḥ śūrasenarāṭ
english: that swift king of the Śūrasenas was consumed in battle, army and all, by Kṛṣṇa the slayer of foes, with Baladeva at his side.

sanskrit: durvāsā nāma viprarṣis tathā paramakopanaḥ ārādhitaḥ sadāreṇa sa cāsmai pradadau varān
english: The brahmin-sage named Durvāsas, of utmost wrath, was propitiated by him together with his wife, and bestowed boons upon him.

sanskrit: tathā gāndhārarājasya sutāṃ vīraḥ svayaṃvare nirjitya pṛthivīpālān avahat puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ
english: So too the lotus-eyed hero, at her self-choosing, vanquished the lords of the earth and bore away the daughter of the king of Gāndhāra.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇā rājāno yasya jātyā hayā iva rathe vaivāhike yuktāḥ pratodena kṛtavraṇāḥ
english: The kings, unable to endure it, were yoked like thoroughbred horses to his wedding chariot and made to bear the wounds of his goad.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdhaṃ mahābāhum upāyena janārdanaḥ pareṇa ghātayām āsa pṛthag akṣauhiṇīpatim
english: Janārdana, by a stratagem, had the mighty-armed Jarāsaṃdha, lord in his own right of a whole akṣauhiṇī, slain by another's hand.

sanskrit: cedirājaṃ ca vikrāntaṃ rājasenāpatiṃ balī arghe vivadamānaṃ ca jaghāna paśuvat tadā
english: And the mighty one then slew like a sacrificial beast the valiant king of the Cedis, that commander of the kings' host, when he disputed the offering of homage.

sanskrit: saubhaṃ daityapuraṃ svasthaṃ śālvaguptaṃ durāsadam samudrakukṣau vikramya pātayām āsa mādhavaḥ
english: Mādhava, charging in, cast down Saubha—that secure city of the daityas, guarded by Śālva and hard to assail—into the belly of the sea.

sanskrit: aṅgān vaṅgān kaliṅgāṃś ca māgadhān kāśikosalān vatsagargakarūṣāṃś ca puṇḍrāṃś cāpy ajayad raṇe
english: He conquered in battle the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, and Kaliṅgas, the Māgadhas, the men of Kāśi and Kosala, the Vatsas, Gargas, and Karūṣas, and the Puṇḍras as well.

sanskrit: āvantyān dākṣiṇātyāṃś ca pārvatīyān daśerakān kāśmīrakān aurasakān piśācāṃś ca samandarān
english: The Āvantyas and the southern peoples, the mountain-dwellers and the Daśerakas, the Kāśmīrakas, the Aurasakas, and the Piśācas with the Mandaras—

sanskrit: kāmbojān vāṭadhānāṃś ca colān pāṇḍyāṃś ca saṃjaya trigartān mālavāṃś caiva daradāṃś ca sudurjayān
english: the Kāmbojas and Vāṭadhānas, the Colas and Pāṇḍyas, Saṃjaya, the Trigartas, the Mālavas, and the Daradas so hard to conquer—

sanskrit: nānādigbhyaś ca saṃprāptān vrātān aśvaśakān prati jitavān puṇḍarīkākṣo yavanāṃś ca sahānugān
english: the lotus-eyed one vanquished too the bands gathered from every quarter, those of the Aśvas and Śakas, and the Yavanas together with their followers.

sanskrit: praviśya makarāvāsaṃ yādobhir abhisaṃvṛtam jigāya varuṇaṃ yuddhe salilāntargataṃ purā
english: Of old, entering the abode of sea-monsters, hemmed about by water-creatures, he conquered Varuṇa in battle within the waters.

sanskrit: yudhi pañcajanaṃ hatvā pātālatalavāsinam pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo divyaṃ śaṅkham avāptavān
english: Having slain in battle Pañcajana, who dwelt in the depths of the netherworld, Hṛṣīkeśa won the divine conch Pāñcajanya.

sanskrit: khāṇḍave pārthasahitas toṣayitvā hutāśanam āgneyam astraṃ durdharṣaṃ cakraṃ lebhe mahābalaḥ
english: At Khāṇḍava, together with Pārtha, the mighty one gratified the Eater of Oblations and obtained the irresistible fiery weapon, the discus.

sanskrit: vainateyaṃ samāruhya trāsayitvāmarāvatīm mahendrabhavanād vīraḥ pārijātam upānayat
english: Mounting the son of Vinatā and striking terror into Amarāvatī, the hero carried off the pārijāta tree from the abode of great Indra.

sanskrit: tac ca marṣitavāñ śakro jānaṃs tasya parākramam rājñāṃ cāpy ajitaṃ kaṃ cit kṛṣṇeneha na śuśruma
english: And Śakra bore that patiently, knowing his prowess; nor have we heard of any king here who was not conquered by Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: yac ca tan mahad āścaryaṃ sabhāyāṃ mama saṃjaya kṛtavān puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ kas tadanya ihārhati
english: And that great marvel which the lotus-eyed one wrought in my assembly hall, Saṃjaya—what other man here is capable of it?

sanskrit: yac ca bhaktyā prapanno 'ham adrākṣaṃ kṛṣṇam īśvaram tan me suviditaṃ sarvaṃ pratyakṣam iva cāgamat
english: And when in devotion I took refuge in him, I beheld Kṛṣṇa as the Lord; all that is well known to me, and came to me as though before my very eyes.

sanskrit: nānto vikramayuktasya buddhyā yuktasya vā punaḥ karmaṇaḥ śakyate gantuṃ hṛṣīkeśasya saṃjaya
english: No end can be reached, Saṃjaya, of the deeds of Hṛṣīkeśa, who is endowed with valor and again with wisdom.

sanskrit: tathā gadaś ca sāmbaś ca pradyumno 'tha vidūrathaḥ āgāvaho 'niruddhaś ca cārudeṣṇaś ca sāraṇaḥ
english: So too Gada and Sāmba, Pradyumna and Viḍūratha, Āgāvaha and Aniruddha, Cārudeṣṇa and Sāraṇa,

sanskrit: ulmuko niśaṭhaś caiva jhallī babhruś ca vīryavān pṛthuś ca vipṛthuś caiva samīko 'thārimejayaḥ
english: Ulmuka and Niśaṭha, Jhallī and the valiant Babhru, Pṛthu and Vipṛthu, Śamīka and Arimejaya—

sanskrit: ete vai balavantaś ca vṛṣṇivīrāḥ prahāriṇaḥ kathaṃ cit pāṇḍavānīkaṃ śrayeyuḥ samare sthitāḥ
english: these mighty Vṛṣṇi heroes, hard-striking warriors, might somehow take their stand with the Pāṇḍava army and abide in the battle.

sanskrit: āhūtā vṛṣṇivīreṇa keśavena mahātmanā tataḥ saṃśayitaṃ sarvaṃ bhaved iti matir mama
english: Summoned by the Vṛṣṇi hero, the high-souled Keśava—then all would be cast into doubt: such is my conviction.

sanskrit: nāgāyutabalo vīraḥ kailāsaśikharopamaḥ vanamālī halī rāmas tatra yatra janārdanaḥ
english: And the hero Rāma, strong as ten thousand elephants, like the peak of Kailāsa, garlanded with wildflowers and bearing the plough, is there where Janārdana is.

sanskrit: yam āhuḥ sarvapitaraṃ vāsudevaṃ dvijātayaḥ api vā hy eṣa pāṇḍūnāṃ yotsyate 'rthāya saṃjaya
english: And he whom the twice-born call Vāsudeva, the father of all—he too, Saṃjaya, may well fight for the cause of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: sa yadā tāta saṃnahyet pāṇḍavārthāya keśavaḥ na tadā pratyanīkeṣu bhavitā tasya kaś cana
english: When Keśava arms himself, my son, for the sake of the Pāṇḍavas, then there will be no one among the opposing ranks to stand against him.

sanskrit: yadi sma kuravaḥ sarve jayeyuḥ sarvapāṇḍavān vārṣṇeyo 'rthāya teṣāṃ vai gṛhṇīyāc chastram uttamam
english: Were all the Kurus to conquer all the Pāṇḍavas, the Vārṣṇeya would surely take up his supreme weapon for their sake.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvān naravyāghro hatvā narapatīn raṇe kauravāṃś ca mahābāhuḥ kuntyai dadyāt sa medinīm
english: Then that tiger among men, the mighty-armed one, having slain in battle all the lords of men and the Kauravas, would give the earth to Kuntī.

sanskrit: yasya yantā hṛṣīkeśo yoddhā yasya dhanaṃjayaḥ rathasya tasya kaḥ saṃkhye pratyanīko bhaved rathaḥ
english: The chariot whose driver is Hṛṣīkeśa and whose warrior is Dhanaṃjaya—what chariot in the field could be its match?

sanskrit: na kena cid upāyena kurūṇāṃ dṛśyate jayaḥ tasmān me sarvam ācakṣva yathā yuddham avartata
english: By no means whatsoever do I see victory for the Kurus; therefore tell me all, just as the battle came to pass.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ keśavasyātmā kṛṣṇo 'py ātmā kirīṭinaḥ arjune vijayo nityaṃ kṛṣṇe kīrtiś ca śāśvatī
english: Arjuna is the very soul of Keśava, and Kṛṣṇa too is the soul of the Diademed one; in Arjuna victory dwells forever, and in Kṛṣṇa undying renown.

sanskrit: prādhānyena hi bhūyiṣṭham ameyāḥ keśave guṇāḥ mohād duryodhanaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ yan na vettīha mādhavam
english: For preeminently and beyond all measure do the virtues abound in Keśava; yet out of delusion Duryodhana does not know Kṛṣṇa, the Mādhava, here in this world.

sanskrit: mohito daivayogena mṛtyupāśapuraskṛtaḥ na veda kṛṣṇaṃ dāśārham arjunaṃ caiva pāṇḍavam
english: Deluded by the working of fate, with the noose of death set before him, he knows neither Kṛṣṇa of the Dāśārha line nor Arjuna the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: pūrvadevau mahātmānau naranārāyaṇāv ubhau ekātmānau dvidhābhūtau dṛśyete mānavair bhuvi
english: Those two high-souled primeval gods, Nara and Nārāyaṇa both, one in soul yet become twofold, are seen by men upon the earth.

sanskrit: manasāpi hi durdharṣau senām etāṃ yaśasvinau nāśayetām ihecchantau mānuṣatvāt tu necchataḥ
english: Those two glorious and irresistible ones could, if they wished, destroy this army by a mere thought; but being in human form, they do not wish it.

sanskrit: yugasyeva viparyāso lokānām iva mohanam bhīṣmasya ca vadhas tāta droṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: The slaying of Bhīṣma, my son, and of the high-souled Droṇa is like the overturning of an age, like the bewildering of the worlds.

sanskrit: na hy eva brahmacaryeṇa na vedādhyayanena ca na kriyābhir na śastreṇa mṛtyoḥ kaś cid vimucyate
english: For not by continence, nor by the study of the Vedas, nor by rites, nor by weapons is any man freed from death.

sanskrit: lokasaṃbhāvitau vīrau kṛtāstrau yuddhadurmadau bhīṣmadroṇau hatau śrutvā kiṃ nu jīvāmi saṃjaya
english: Hearing that Bhīṣma and Droṇa are slain—those two heroes honored by the world, masters of arms, unconquerable in the fury of battle—why should I go on living, Saṃjaya?
